Thousands of people in Hong Kong gathered for a #MeToo rally following claims that police sexually assaulted some pro-democracy protesters.

Last week a protester said she was unnecessarily strip searched and another said her skirt was flipped up as police carried her away. https://t.co/bw8rpIZkdW

@JenLouiseWilson Venice recently announced a 2019 seminar on “Gender Equality and Inclusivity and Film Industry.” The two-hour event was organized by Women in Film, Television & Media Italy, Dissenso Comune (Italy’s #MeToo equivalent) & other film funding bodies. (5/10)
https://t.co/JkTNt8xCk6

A Paris court ordered the woman who launched France's answer to #MeToo to pay $16.5K in damages for defamation to a man she says made lewd comments to her.

He says he did make them but he apologized via text.

Sandra Muller said: "The message that is being sent is 'shut up.'" https://t.co/pW6b4MBYFP

#MeToo founder Tarana Burke launched a voter movement called #MeTooVoter — saying 2020 candidates haven't done enough to tackle sexual violence or involve survivors.

"We need these candidates to see us as a power base. So many people engage with survivors from a place of pity." https://t.co/zZR3kp31Eo
